reviews.title: Not worth subscription
reviews.text: Premium subscription is extremely difficult to cancel - you must jump through hoops on the website rather than through the app or Apple. Customer service is unhelpful, and you continue to get ads while being subscribed to premium. You cannot cancel through apple or you will continue to be charged, and even if you click through the app and manage to find your transaction history, it will not include dates, which is very frustrating. You can’t even cancel within the app, only on the external developer’s website. Premium features are fine if you can get discount, but certainly not worth the money or headache especially considering annual billing means they will likely get an extra year’s payment out of you. So many features have also gotten so much worse in the last year. After some research, it looks like this subscription model may be against Apple’s policies, so other users leaving negative reviews about similar experiences should make a report to Apple as well.

reviews.title: Less marketing. Less data. More actionable guidance. That’s what would make this worth paying for
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app, but after paying for an annual subscription I found it disappointing.

The biggest issue is that I received more notifications encouraging me to upgrade to a lifetime subscription than notifications that actually helped me improve my health. It often feels like the app is trying to sell me something rather than coach me.

The amount of data is overwhelming, but very little of it is translated into clear, actionable advice. I don’t need dozens of graphs and scores—I need to know what to do today. Should I train or recover? Have I done enough exercise? What should I focus on to improve my cardiovascular health?

For an app that claims to provide AI-powered health insights, I expected practical guidance rather than information overload.

The concept is excellent, but the execution left me feeling that I paid for a dashboard full of metrics instead of a health coach. Unfortunately, I can’t recommend the annual subscription based on my experience.

reviews.title: Was great until I paid
reviews.text:
The app was great, I had a recent TIA and was using the app to provide much needed critical information for my health. I thought it would be beneficial to save a little money since this was going to be something I utilized often. I paid for the annual application and received the information I want to know about. About a month later I started getter my messages, emailed and even in app notifications that I needed to upgrade to lifetime membership to get more of my collected info. This seems awful to me that this is not something anyone is aware of until the y hook you into the first expensive purchase. Anyone that has made a lifetime purchase in the past, then finds out the company is closing loses the purchase. Like 23and me. Pay for the lifetime lose your
Money. 

Don’t let this fool you the app has a benefit, I still use it. It still helps but unfortunately monetization of your information never ends. Your health is parsed out to you as they collect it continually. I am not going to pay for the lifetime info, I am not going to renew and I am going to request my information be deleted when I am done with the year.

A year later my premium subscription expired at the beginning of May and suddenly according to the app I am basically dying again and have to upgrade to get the details. No doubt if I upgrade my health will be perfect again. The app itself is excellent but this practice of severe health issues if you are not on premium should be reported and stopped.

reviews.title: Buyer beware
reviews.text: I saw this app and it looked very promising as a way to get additional insights into my health data. It is entirely AI driven and not in a good and reliable way. The data and reporting often conflicts with the data in my Apple health app, or is just wrong. You are also bombarded with ads to upgrade to lifetime membership, even if you’re a premium subscriber. You can’t turn this off! I finally decided I’d had enough and wanted to cancel. First, none of their cancellation methods worked. Then, it took me well over a week of back-and-forth with their customer support to get them to confirm that my membership had been canceled and it would not auto renew. Then when I went into the app to try and delete my data and account, I was told that I could not do that until my subscription ended “for my own protection.” So, I had to get back on with customer support again and ask them to manually convert my account from a paid subscription to an unpaid subscription so that I could delete my account and then put in a dated deletion request. Needless to say I do not recommend this app.

reviews.title: I’ve paid for premium remove the adds
reviews.text: I quite like this product, enough to have moved from the free limited version to an annual subscription that did open up some other stuff… However my view of the results is constantly blocked by another advert asking me to increase my premium subscription to a premium lifetime subscription. I don’t want to do this. I don’t have the money.. I can’t find any way to remove this advert from my paid subscription. The distraction is enough to make me consider taking the app off my phone. This is not a way to treat a paying customer..

reviews.title: Aesthetic Paywall Gimick
reviews.text:
It looks nice, pretty colours, they want you to hunt the green bars and charts. The actual measurements they take such as HRV etc. are inconsistently taken, and misinterpreted. Their algorithm is simplistic and doesn’t understand the information fed to it properly. You hit a 1000 calorie workout and it shows -1% battery, -2% stress. Every, single, time. It says your ‘health rating’ is 56 and stress level 100, but then you do a manual measurement and suddenly your health is 100% and stress level 30%.

Also there is ALWAYS some kind of discount running, which they push relentlessly at you ie. 66% off for more detailed insights. If the discount is always running it’s not a discount, it’s a marketing tactic t squeeze more money out of you. If you’re serious about training and your health avoid.

They drag you in with the aesthetic, hook you with the dopamine hit you get from the pretty colours, then offer constant special deals and discounts to make you pay for an even more premium version than you’re already on.

reviews.title: Unhealthy health monitor
reviews.text: I originally subscribed to this app because I loved how much it could tell me about my health, sleep, and stress. It initially motivated me to work out and keep up with my goals. However, with recent updates including the exercise tracking via Mets, I’ve found that the goals are completely unreasonable and unhealthy to achieve. Despite working out for an hour and a half per day achieving heart rate goals in the moderate to hard range, the app will continue to tell you that you have not worked out enough. The more you try to appease the app (eg no rest days, longer and harder workouts), the higher the bar will get, making it impossible to achieve these goals unless you are targeting max HR for over an hour, which in itself is incredibly unhealthy. I have recently cancelled my subscription because I have unfortunately come to terms that this app is completely detrimental to my mental health and physical wellbeing. I hope someone re-evaluates these goals and works with their algorithm to make them more realistic and balanced before someone gets hurt in a misguided attempt to appease an AI bot. For context, I am a young adult who lifts 30 min/ day in addition to cardio 45-60 min/ day.
